findings.reason: it changes which file gets the change, removes a fourth call site instead of adding one, and makes the wrapper in §2 unnecessary.
findings.text: `admission_domain_findings` is the existing shared admission-finding composer and it already runs on BOTH paths the plan calls "the single path" and "the batch path": `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:911` → `reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:2019` (inside `_require_write_paths_in_authority`; the single path separately splits its sandbox findings through the same helper at `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:977`) and `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:323` (`admission_domain_findings(node, project=…, repository=repo_root)` inside `queue_requests`, which `queue_batch` reaches at `reckon/crew/dispatch_batch.py:575`). §2 instead proposes a new function "in `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py`" — i.e. a fifth composer in a fourth module — over a channel that is already shared, already returns `dict[str, str]` findings, and is already split into refusals and warnings by `admission_refusals_and_warnings` at `reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:1961`. Extend that owner (it takes `node`, `project`, `repository`, and can take `locked_decisions`/`budget_ceiling`) rather than forking it

findings.reason: a shared function that does not subsume `queue_edit._contract_findings` leaves a third copy that can drift, which is the exact defect §2 exists to remove.
findings.text: a third site already carries out §2's stated goal of judging a stored node under the same locked decisions and budget ceiling the launch will use: `_contract_findings` (lines 164-184) calls `validate_node(node, locked_decisions=tuple(options.get("locked_decisions") or ()), budget_ceiling=resolved_time_ceiling(_resolve_lane_config(record)))` against a queued request record. §2 describes "the same locked decisions, budget ceiling and repository path" as a new requirement and never mentions this existing implementation, so the census of sites that enforce the node contract is short by one (`repeat: dispatch_plan.py:843`, `queue_edit.py:179`, and the batch's `dispatch.py:323`)

findings.reason: §2's deliverable would build a third path for a refusal that is one argument away from being centralised in `validate_node`.
findings.text: §2 says "The fourth refusal, execution fit (`dispatch_plan.py` near line 869), is shared as well", but `validate_node` already accepts `execution_capable` and performs exactly that refusal at `reckon/crew/node.py:1255-1262` (`capability.assess_execution_fit(...); if fit.conflict: fail("fully-specified", fit.refusal_detail())`), projecting the same `refusal_detail()` into the same `property: fully-specified` shape `dispatch_plan.py:869-879` builds by hand. `dispatch_plan.py:843` calls `validate_node` WITHOUT passing `execution_capable`, so the parameter is dead on the only path that would use it (`reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:746` calls `assess_execution_fit` a third time). The honest change is one line — pass `execution_capable=backend.get("execution_capable")` at `dispatch_plan.py:843` and delete the duplicate block at 837/869-879 — not new machinery to "share" a check that has two homes already

findings.reason: the section's done-when must enumerate every required field of each op, or it ships a half-fix that the plan's own rationale says is the problem.
findings.text: §1 and §4 both give `close` as raising on `status` then `by`, but `_apply_close` checks three required fields in sequence: `status` (4142-4147), `outcome` (4148-4151) and `by` (4152-4154). §4's done-when is "`close` with neither `status` nor `by` is refused naming both", which passes while still revealing `outcome` alone on the next round trip — the defect the section removes for two fields and leaves standing for a third. Same census gap for `append_evidence`: the six required fields at `_store.py:1283-1306` are `plan`, `anchor`, `title`, `body` plus two format constraints on `plan` and `anchor` that a collector must decide whether to merge into one message

findings.reason: extending `validate_node` (or `admission_domain_findings`) removes the duplicated `NodeValidation(ok=False, findings=[*verdict.findings, …])` composition repeated three times at `dispatch_plan.py:851-879`, which a wrapper leaves in place.
findings.text: the function §2 proposes is a wrapper: it forwards to `validate_node` (node.py:1182), `negative_control_finding` (node.py:1054), `gate_population_finding` (node.py:1145) and `assess_execution_fit` (capability.py:106) and adds no behaviour of its own; §2 gives no reason the existing shared owner (`admission_domain_findings`) or `validate_node` itself cannot be extended with the two extra findings (`negative_control_finding` and `gate_population_finding` both take a `TaskNode` and return the same `dict[str, str]` shape). `validate_node` is already the documented "judge a node against all eight properties, reporting every failure" entry point and already reports findings cumulatively

findings.reason: the section must either name what it retires (a flag now redundant with the recorded value) or state why all four flag positions must exist.
findings.text: §3 adds `--plan-link` and `--unplanned-reason` to `crew dispatch` (two more of the 465 CLI options) plus a new `TaskNode` field, and its text names nothing it retires, merges or replaces; the same two flags already exist on `crew complete` and `crew merge` (`reckon/crew_run_commands.py:237-238`, `2899-2916`) and are already mapped flag→record in `reckon/crew/obligations.py:246-247`, and the pointer's `dispatch_options` dict (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:354`) is already the carrier a dispatch-time value would ride to landing, so one of the two options could be retired in favour of reading the stored value

findings.reason: if the fence already runs on the shared `plan_dispatch`, the true defect is in authority resolution and §5's deliverable as written would add a second call site instead of fixing the first.
findings.text: §5 proposes making `--dry-run` "run that check", but the dry run already reaches it: `crew_dispatch_commands.py:1915` calls `crew_module.plan_dispatch(... repo=repo ...)`, the same function the real launch calls, and `_require_write_paths_in_authority` sits at `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:911` inside `if verdict.ok and repo is not None`. The fence is also already exercised through `plan_dispatch` in `tests/test_crew.py:1461-1470` (`test_non_repository_delivery_directories_are_valid_exclusive_scopes`), alongside the `crew.dispatch` refusal test at 1433-1454. So "`--dry-run` runs that check" may describe a state that already holds, and the reproduction §5 demands is the right first step — but the section pre-commits the repair location before that reproduction, and must name the escaping condition (`verdict.ok` false? a `repo` that resolves elsewhere? an `authority` argument the CLI omits at 1915 that `dispatch()` passes at 692?)

§2 now passes execution_capable to validate_node at dispatch_plan.py near line 843 and deletes the hand-built execution-fit block near lines 837 and 869-879, since validate_node already performs that refusal.
§4 now enumerates every required field: close's status, outcome and by; append_evidence's plan, anchor, title and body plus the plan and anchor format checks; append's target.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no new module is proposed; §4 extends `reckon/_store.py` in place, §5 extends `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py` in place, and §2's consolidation, if placed on the existing owner, removes call sites rather than adding a subsystem. The shallowness of §2's proposed function is carried by the `thin_wrapper` and `duplicate_owner` findings below rather than restated here.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan re-implements the shared contract-composition mechanism rather than extending its owner `reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:1939`, and proposes a "shared as well" home for the execution-fit refusal that `reckon/crew/node.py:1255-1262` already implements inside `validate_node`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 2360, cli_options 465, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 23; §3 adds two CLI options (`--plan-link`, `--unplanned-reason` on `crew dispatch`) and a new node field without naming anything it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites no search of `reckon/crew/` before proposing a new shared contract function, and it misses the owner that is already shared by both paths (`reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:1939` `admission_domain_findings`, called from `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:323` and, on the single path, from `reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:2019` under `dispatch_plan.py:911`) and the third existing enforcement site (`reckon/crew/queue_edit.py:164` `_contract_findings`); it also surveys `_store.py` incompletely, missing one of the three required fields `close` checks.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §2's "one function in `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py` that both paths call" adds a fourth composer over four findings composers that already exist and are already callable from both paths, and justifies nothing about why the shared owner cannot be extended.
